title: Fix the sefaria_ref_matcher_test.dart sortOrder test that cannot verify its own claim
rule: TQ-8 (assertion must match what the source can actually do wrong)

evidence.quote: // Sets don't preserve insertion order, but the function sorts before

why: leafChildrenForContainer returns Set<String>, so any internal sort is erased before the caller sees it; the test's own comment admits this and falls back to containsAll (membership only, no order check), so the test cannot fail if the production sort() call were deleted entirely — its name promises an ordering guarantee the assertion never checks.
recommendation: Rename the test to describe what it actually checks (all three leaves present), or — if callers genuinely depend on order (resolveIndexedUnitRefs re-sorts independently, suggesting they don't) — change the return type to an ordered List and assert order for real.
acceptance_criteria: Test name matches its assertion, or the assertion is strengthened to check real order via a List-returning API.

corrections: Minor imprecision in the finding's framing: Dart's .toSet() actually returns a LinkedHashSet, which preserves insertion order (the sort isn't literally 'erased'), but this doesn't matter — containsAll ignores order regardless, so the core 'test can't catch a missing sort' claim still holds.
